description: ROS 2 (Jazzy / Humble) Python node layer — MinimalPublisher (Twist → /cmd_vel at 2 Hz) + MinimalSubscriber (/odom → Odometry) + bringup.launch.py. Wires ament_python entry_points; ready to colcon build after sourcing the ROS overlay.

buildHints.whenToUse: Attach for any ROS 2 Python node — mobile robots, manipulators, sensor bridges, Nav2 lifecycle nodes. Pick this over ros2-node-rust unless the prompt specifically asks for Rust / rclrs or hard-realtime.
firstSteps: Source the ROS 2 overlay: `source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash` (swap jazzy→humble for 22.04). rclpy is NOT pip-installable — it ships with the apt distribution.
Place the composed project at `<ws>/src/{{packageName}}` — the directory containing package.xml must be directly under src/.
From workspace root: `colcon build --packages-select {{packageName}} && source install/setup.bash`
Run the minimal node: `ros2 run {{packageName}} my_node`
Run publisher: `ros2 run {{packageName}} publisher` — publishes Twist to /cmd_vel at 2 Hz.
Run subscriber in a second terminal (after sourcing install/setup.bash): `ros2 run {{packageName}} subscriber` — prints /odom pose.
Or launch both together: `ros2 launch {{packageName}} bringup.launch.py`
gotchas: rclpy is not pip-installable — source /opt/ros/{{rosDistro}}/setup.bash so the apt-installed rclpy lands on PYTHONPATH before calling colcon.
setup.py entry_points['console_scripts'] is the ONLY way `ros2 run <pkg> <script>` discovers executables. A missing or misspelled entry = silent missing script with no warning.
resource/{{packageName}} is a mandatory empty ament index marker — deleting it breaks `ros2 pkg list` and makes the package invisible to the ROS graph.

Launch files must appear under share/{{packageName}}/launch after install. If `ros2 launch` can't find bringup.launch.py, inspect install/{{packageName}}/share/{{packageName}}/launch — data_files in setup.py drives this mapping.
Re-source install/setup.bash after every colcon build — ROS overlays are not auto-applied like nvm/pyenv. Forgetting this is the #1 cause of 'package not found' after a rebuild.
ROS_DOMAIN_ID defaults to 0, meaning all nodes on the subnet see each other's topics. Set `export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=<1-232>` per workstation in any shared-network environment.
Topic names in the node code are relative (e.g. `cmd_vel`, not `/cmd_vel`) so they respect node namespacing and remapping. Absolute names (/cmd_vel) break multi-robot namespace isolation.
architectureNotes: MinimalPublisher owns the rclpy timer and publishes independently of subscribers — _tick must stay non-blocking (no sleeps, no I/O waits).
MinimalSubscriber is stateless; extend _on_odom to accumulate pose into a shared dict or write to a ROS parameter for multi-node coordination.
For Nav2 integration, inherit from rclpy.lifecycle.LifecycleNode and wire on_configure / on_activate callbacks — a plain Node subclass won't participate in bt_navigator lifecycle management.

placeholders.description: Replace 'my_ros2_node' with your actual ROS 2 package name — must match the directory name, setup.py package_name, and the resource marker filename.

Minimal node stub — 'my_ros2_node' is a placeholder package name. Replace MyNode class body with your actual node logic: add publishers, subscribers, timers, action clients, or service servers as needed.
Publishes a fixed Twist (linear.x=0.1, angular.z=0.2). Replace the _tick body with real velocity commands from a planner, joystick axis, or control loop output.
Logs /odom pose to screen. Replace _on_odom with your localization state update, dead-reckoning accumulator, or Nav2 feedback handler.
Launches publisher + subscriber as separate processes. Add more Node() actions here as the robot grows (e.g. costmap server, joystick driver, SLAM node).
